jobs.title: ESE Teacher at Charter Schools USA
jobs.description: Employer: Charter Schools USA Expires: 08/22/2026 ESE TEACHERCharter Schools USA (CSUSA) Who We AreCharter Schools USA (CSUSA) is one of the largest and highest ­performing education management companies in the United States, proudly serving over 82,000 students in over 150 schools in four states. Founded by Jonathan Hage in 1997, CSUSA's mission is a Relentless Commitment to Student Greatness in School and in Life™. CSUSA provides an academically rigorous education to students equipping them with real world readiness, prepared for college or career after graduation. With an unwavering dedication to the success of students from every background, CSUSA is closing the gaps in achievement and opportunity, keeping our promise of Strong Minds, Good Hearts™. Job PurposeTo join a team of people with the mission: Relentless Commitment to Student Greatness in School and in Life ™. If you love inspiring and motivating young learners and want to put students first in education, CSUSA is the right place for you. We deliver on our promise of Strong Minds, Good Hearts™ through an education model that gives every student the opportunity for success. As an ESE Teacher, you will work in partnership with parents, students, and regular education teachers in accordance with the school's mission and vision in order to promote student achievement. The following responsibilities and duties are the means to achieve that end while maintaining compliance with Federal and State Regulations. How You Will Impact EducationPrepares for and conducts Parent and student conferencing according to school policy.Delivers student instruction in modalities instituted by the school and assigned program (may include but are not limited to: Individual or Group Direct Synchronous Instruction, Learning Support, Life Skills Support, Itinerant Support, Resource Room Support, co-teaching, writing lesson plans, telephone conferencing and instruction, Parent Learning Opportunities).Collects data and appropriate work samples.Plans and conducts appointments with parents as needed.Assists regular education teachers with specially designed instruction when necessary.Participates at monthly outings encouraged.Provides support for ESE student achievement in the general class through training teachers and assisting with the implementation of school inclusion plans.Arranges for and assists with training for inclusionary practices.Acts as an informational liaison for inclusion as appropriate.Assists with planning for classroom and testing accommodations for students with disabilities.Models' strategies for inclusionary practices as appropriate.Provides assistance with developing and adapting curriculum materials and educational practices to meet the needs of students and teachers. Monitoring and ComplianceCollaborates with regular education teachers to monitor student progress and compliance (including student compliance issues, withdrawals, etc.).Proctors standardized tests.Completes student progress reports four times a year (quarterly). Special Education ResponsibilitiesMaintains IEPs, Quarterly Reports, Progress Monitoring for caseload.Develops and Implements IEPs with measurable goals using Progress Monitoring.Collects and Reports Progress Monitoring Data for all student goals.Conduct IEP meetings within timelines.Makes data-driven instructional decisions to improve student outcomes.Completes Quarterly Progress Reports.Maintains accurate and compliant special education data (class lists with contact info, related services info, IEP due dates, etc.).Completes reevaluations in accordance with Regulations and best practices.Completes all special education paperwork accurately, according to regulations, and on time.Develops and monitors appropriate transition plans for students of transition age.Maintains communication with Related Service Providers and Case Managers to ensure compliance with the provision of services, evaluations, and quarterly progress reports.Administers diagnostic assessments as needed.Obtains and maintains compliant special education student files.Participates in State specific training.Attends Professional Development as designated on the school calendar (travel may be required). CommunicationCommunicates with Regular Education Teachers and Administrators when necessary.Participates in weekly team meetings.Acknowledge e-mails and voice mails within 24 hours (excluding weekends, holidays, etc.). Required Qualifications and SkillsDemonstrates enthusiasm and commitment toward the position and the mission of the company; support the company's values in the strategic areas of academic excellence, operational performance, superior culture, and financial health and growth, as outlined in the Employee Handbook.Possesses strong time management & organizational skills and the ability to prioritize effectively.Has the ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with teachers, students, parents, the community, and administrative staff. Is sensitive to sensitive to corporate needs, employee goodwill, and the public image, as unique situations present themselves.Possesses excellent interpersonal skills and displays such between all stakeholders: being courteous, professional, and helpful.Possesses excellent communication skills: Oral (including presentations), Written, Interpersonal (active listening), Negotiating and Influencing.Has the ability to be at work consistently, to be on time, to follow instructions, to respond to management direction and to solicit feedback to improve performance.Demonstrates proficient experience with Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint), Student Information System (SIS) and email communications.Looks for ways to improve and promote quality and demonstrates accuracy and thoroughness.Strives to implement best practices and positive character education consistently. jobs.description: Employer: Tutor Corps Expires: 08/22/2026 NOW HIRING · K-12 · FULLY REMOTE · COAST TO COASTOne student. One teacher. Real learning.Pacific Preparatory is a Cognia-accredited K-12 virtual school built around one idea: every student deserves a teacher who actually knows them.The roleWe are looking for educators who want flexible, hourly remote work and who have the availability and the commitment to build a genuine caseload of students over time. We provide both tutoring and teaching opportunities to help build your caseload, as we also offer a robust after-school and summer tutoring program.At Pacific Prep, you will teach one-on-one, and you will receive an individualized syllabus for each student, a working draft we build specifically for that learner that you take and make your own. We mail you the books and hands-on materials directly, so you are never buying curriculum or building lessons from scratch. You bring the relationship, the instincts, and the craft, and we take care of the rest.Our students span K-12, and most instructors specialize in a subject area, a grade band, or both. Within your area of expertise, you will work with a range of students and learning profiles, and the role asks you to stay curious about the individual in front of you, whether that is a third grader building foundational reading skills or a twelfth grader finishing coursework before a gap year. You will get to know very different kids within your subject area, and that variety is a feature of this job, not a side effect of it.We hold a high standard on both sides of this role, the teaching and the follow-through, which means being responsive to families, completing session notes and admin on time, and showing up prepared. We will give you everything you need to meet that standard, and we ask you to actually meet it.Who we are looking forWe hire on a rolling basis and are always looking to add excellent educators to our roster. Here is who we are looking for.A former classroom teacher, professor, curriculum writer, or long-term private instructor who is ready for something more flexible and more remote, including credentialed teachers with current or expired teaching credentials.Someone with at least 15 hours of open availability Monday through Friday, whether during school hours, after-school hours, or both, who is ready to fill that time with a growing caseload of students.A person who cares about doing excellent work and follows through on all of it: the teaching, the admin, and the ongoing relationship with each student and family.Genuine comfort with learner variability, including gifted students, students with learning differences, and students navigating complex circumstances, and a real belief that knowing each student individually is the most important part of the job.Background in AP courses, AP exams, standardized test prep (SAT, ACT, SSAT, ISEE, HSTP), and Executive Functioning support is ideal for educators wanting to join our tutoring program.Experience working with students with learning differences is strongly preferred, and candidates with special education credentials or structured literacy training are especially encouraged to apply.Curiosity about reading new books and working through new subjects, including a willingness to learn the material right alongside your students when it is unfamiliar to you.A bachelor's degree or higher and at least two years of teaching or instructional experience.Confidence on Zoom and with digital tools, because you work from home and you know how to make it feel like a classroom.What we offerStarting rates at $25+ per hour for 100% remote work with biannual raise cycles and regular opportunities for bonuses. Select in person opportunities in SF Bay Area and LA.Paid prep time.Individualized syllabi and all student materials provided, including books, hands-on supplies, and resources mailed directly to you at no cost.We handle all student matching and billing so you can focus on teaching.Professional development, coaching, and ongoing support from our academic team. We are invested in you as a teacher, not just in filling your schedule.A community of educators who are doing the same kind of work and understand what it involves.Growth potential: instructors who perform well receive regular raises, and long-tenured teachers can earn $3,000 or more per month.What to expectPacific Preparatory is a school, not a marketplace. You will have dedicated students, ongoing relationships, and a team behind you. Your schedule can include for-credit courses, academic tutoring, or a mix of both, and we will work with you to build a caseload that fits your availability and your strengths. What we are looking for is educators who are ready to show up consistently for their students, and who bring the same standard to every session whether it is a formal course or a tutoring engagement. If that sounds like you, we want to hear from you.$25+ per hour · 15+ hrs/week availability · 100% remoteApply at pacificpreparatory.org/about/join-our-teamPacific Preparatory is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building a diverse, inclusive team. Employment decisions are based on qualifications, not race, religion, gender, age, orientation, or other protected characteristics. jobs.description: Employer: FairField Center Expires: 08/22/2026 Mediation Case Manager (Lead) Hours per week = 40 Pay = $17/hr. Paid time off available. The FairField Center has been a pillar in the Shenandoah Valley since 1982 as the first community mediation center in Virginia. The center is committed to the just resolution of conflicts by empowering individuals and communities to live and work together peacefully. POSITION SUMMARY CASE MANAGEMENT: Provide case management and oversee case management services for FairField’s court-referred (and other-referred) mediation services. Case management includes: Intake and screening interviews (May be by telephone, in-person, or electronic mediums). Gathering relevant information from potential clients, explaining the mediation process, and assessing appropriateness. Scheduling: Matching times clients are available for mediation with appropriately qualified mediators and, as needed, observers; completing reminder calls and emails. Cases must be assigned to mediators in a fair and equitable manner based on the mediators’ schedules, availability, and abilities with regard to specific case types. Preparation: Placing forms in case files; assigning cases to mediation rooms; checking mediation rooms for conditions and necessary materials, sending video conference links as needed, and greeting mediators and clients when they arrive. Follow-up: Rescheduling cases; processing agreements, contacting clients for follow-up on agreement status, documenting and filing case outcome with the Courts as needed. Data collection: Maintaining the details of case events by entering and updating data into databases; providing data to the Executive Director and courts as needed. Reporting and billing: Attending court as needed, completing court reports, and billing and invoicing. Evaluation: Reviewing mediator evaluations and sharing any client concerns with the service provider and Executive Director Quality Control: The lead case manager must maintain a roster of certified mediators who meet the qualification requirements established by the court. The manager ensures that mediation services provided through the FairField Center are of high quality. Managers are under no obligation to accept a new roster request, however, the manager should strive to achieve a large and diverse cadre of mediators to best accommodate the needs of parties. SUPPORT SERVICES: Oversee responses to phone calls, be familiar with the other FairField services, ensure forms are restocked as necessary, and perform other office duties as necessary. MEDIATION TRAINING AND PARTICIPATION: Participate in trainings, role plays, and attend mediations as an observer or co‑mediator during mediation sessions as available, MEDIATION CERTIFICATION: Hold or obtain Virginia mediation certification in General District Court (GDC) and Juvenile and Domestic Relations Court (JDR). Enroll in the certification process within 6 months to be completed within the certification window. The Lead Case Manager is the only full-time case manager, so the following qualifications are important: REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS: Self-motivated, detail-oriented, and able to handle stressful situations (de-escalation skills) Able to collaborate with individuals and teams in a professional setting Computer fluency, able to learn and maintain databases and work with new technologies as required. Able to work at the FairField Center’s Harrisonburg, VA office PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS: English and Spanish speaking Position Details: Reports to: Executive Director Location: 60 S. High St., Harrisonburg, VA Application Instructions: Interested applicants should send a resume, cover letter, and two professional references to Noel Levan at noel_levan@hotmail.com and Christine Poulson at christine@fairfieldcenter.org. The position will remain open until a suitable candidate is found. FairField Center is committed to providing equal opportunity for all without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, marital status, sexual orientation, disability, political aﬃliation, personal appearance, family responsibilities, matriculation or any other characteristic protected under federal, state, or local law. The FairField Center is a drug-free workplace.

jobs.feedName: Michael D. Eisner College of Education
jobs.title: Behavior Technician at The Language and Behavior Center
jobs.description: Employer: The Language and Behavior Center Expires: 08/22/2026 Position OverviewOur Behavior Technicians (BT) work as a part of the ABA Treatment Team, providing in-home services for children with Autism and related disorders. Our BTs receive frequent supervision and support from a supervising BCBA. They're integral to the child's progress as well as family communication with the ABA Treatment Team. The BTs role involves planning, collecting data, and treatment.Planning – BTs are responsible for arriving at appointments with materials to keep clients engaged and stimulated for the duration of the appointment. This can include toys, books, games, arts & crafts, or other creative ideas. Prior to the scheduled session, the BT consults with the child’s supervising BCBA to determine the appropriate goals, materials, and activities for the day’s session.Specific job responsibilities includeReview the child's individualized treatment plan and goals prior to session.Develop a plan for the session, to include creative materials and engaging activities to integrate into programs.Consult with the supervising BCBA to ensure the appointment follows the designed schedule and addresses the child’s individualized goals.Punctuality: BTs are expected to arrive a minimum of 5 minutes prior to the session’s start time.Collecting Data – BTs need to collect data in order to monitor the progress and effectiveness of the individualized treatment plan. Regular and ongoing data collection is vital in evaluating the progress a client makes towards their goals. Critical decisions regarding the client’s goals and therapy sessions are made based on this ongoing data collection. BTs will collect their data during sessions as they implement programs developed by the supervising BCBA. This allows the ABA and administrative team to ensure the treatment is progressing and effective.Specific job responsibilities includeCollect data throughout session to actively monitor the child's progressParticipate in program development with the BCBADiscuss collected data with the BCBA and assist with program modifications to ensure the child continues to reach attainable goalsEnsure confidentiality and abide by HIPPA regulationsTreatment – BTs are responsible for implementing the child’s individual treatment goals throughout the session. Specified targets are embedded in play and seamlessly incorporated into fun and engaging activities. BTs collect data on all specified targets and provide a comprehensive, narrative report at the end of each session.Specific job responsibilities includeProvide reliable one-on-one ABA services based on the child's treatment planImplement programs developed by the child’s supervising BCBA to help build communication, advocacy skills, daily living skills, and social-emotional skillsAssist with preference assessment to ensure the child is continually motivated during teachingProvide an overview of the session activities to the caregiver at the end of each sessionObtain a signature from the caregiver at the end of each sessionInclude all specified information on the session note (i.e. caregivers present, start and end time of session, behavior goals, and skill acquisition goals)Ensure confidentiality and abide by HIPPA regulationsAbout The Language and Behavior Center:We provide family-focused therapeutic services to children age 0-12 years old. With a focus on play-based learning, TLBC believes that language and skill development should be a positive experience for both the child and the family.Why Work at TLBC?Local Caseloads: BTs are assigned to clients near where they live, which means less time spent in the car and more time spent with clients.Social Environment: We have frequent staff get-togethers, clinic meetings, mentorship meetings, and a central office with coffee and snacks always stocked.Technology: TLBC uses electronic data collection. BCBAs are able to make immediate changes to programs and see progress in real-time, which means BTs are always running up-to-date programsStructure for personal growth: BTs are provided with a clear pathway to grow in the ABA field. We also support our BTs' individual interests and provide opportunities for them to pursue these interests at TLBC.Focus on Staff: The happiness of our staff is essential to the quality of service that TLBC provides. TLBC is constantly evolving to ensure our staff's happiness through an extensive benefits package, supportive mentors and supervisors, and frequent opportunities for promotions and raises.What makes you a great fit for TLBC:Enthusiastic about TLBC’s mission and the success of its clientsStrong organization skillsCollaborativeStrong interpersonal skillsExperience working with childrenOpen to obtaining RBT certification within 90 days of employment (training provided)Ability to work afternoons (3:00-6:00pm) a minimum of three days per weekBenefits:The RBT position is a W-2 position with the following benefits for full-time employees:Competitive hourly ratePaid Time OffSick LeaveFlexible hoursMedical Insurance for full-time staff401(k) with a 4% company matchShort-term Disability Insurance for full-time staffInitial as well as Ongoing TrainingIn-house RBT TrainingTablet for Electronic Data CollectionPaid trainingsMileage PayFrequent Support & SupervisionContinuing Education reimbursementAccess to TLBC materials, curriculums, and gamesOpportunities for growth within the companyFor more information about our company or our staff, check out our website at www.tl-bc.comJob Type: Part-timeBenefits: 401(k)401(k) matchingDental insuranceFlexible scheduleHealth insurancePaid time offTuition reimbursementVision insurance

jobs.description: Employer: The Language and Behavior Center Expires: 08/22/2026 Position OverviewOur Behavior Technicians (BT) work as a part of the ABA Treatment Team, providing in-home services for children with Autism and related disorders. Our BTs receive frequent supervision and support from a supervising BCBA. They're integral to the child's progress as well as family communication with the ABA Treatment Team. The BTs role involves planning, collecting data, and treatment.Planning – BTs are responsible for arriving at appointments with materials to keep clients engaged and stimulated for the duration of the appointment. This can include toys, books, games, arts & crafts, or other creative ideas. Prior to the scheduled session, the BT consults with the child’s supervising BCBA to determine the appropriate goals, materials, and activities for the day’s session.Specific job responsibilities includeReview the child's individualized treatment plan and goals prior to session.Develop a plan for the session, to include creative materials and engaging activities to integrate into programs.Consult with the supervising BCBA to ensure the appointment follows the designed schedule and addresses the child’s individualized goals.Punctuality: BTs are expected to arrive a minimum of 5 minutes prior to the session’s start time.Collecting Data – BTs need to collect data in order to monitor the progress and effectiveness of the individualized treatment plan. Regular and ongoing data collection is vital in evaluating the progress a client makes towards their goals. Critical decisions regarding the client’s goals and therapy sessions are made based on this ongoing data collection. BTs will collect their data during sessions as they implement programs developed by the supervising BCBA. This allows the ABA and administrative team to ensure the treatment is progressing and effective.Specific job responsibilities includeCollect data throughout session to actively monitor the child's progressParticipate in program development with the BCBADiscuss collected data with the BCBA and assist with program modifications to ensure the child continues to reach attainable goalsEnsure confidentiality and abide by HIPPA regulationsTreatment – BTs are responsible for implementing the child’s individual treatment goals throughout the session. Specified targets are embedded in play and seamlessly incorporated into fun and engaging activities. BTs collect data on all specified targets and provide a comprehensive, narrative report at the end of each session.Specific job responsibilities includeProvide reliable one-on-one ABA services based on the child's treatment planImplement programs developed by the child’s supervising BCBA to help build communication, advocacy skills, daily living skills, and social-emotional skillsAssist with preference assessment to ensure the child is continually motivated during teachingProvide an overview of the session activities to the caregiver at the end of each sessionObtain a signature from the caregiver at the end of each sessionInclude all specified information on the session note (i.e. caregivers present, start and end time of session, behavior goals, and skill acquisition goals)Ensure confidentiality and abide by HIPPA regulationsAbout The Language and Behavior Center:We provide family-focused therapeutic services to children age 0-12 years old. With a focus on play-based learning, TLBC believes that language and skill development should be a positive experience for both the child and the family.Why Work at TLBC?Local Caseloads: BTs are assigned to clients near where they live, which means less time spent in the car and more time spent with clients.Social Environment: We have frequent staff get-togethers, clinic meetings, mentorship meetings, and a central office with coffee and snacks always stocked.Technology: TLBC uses electronic data collection. BCBAs are able to make immediate changes to programs and see progress in real-time, which means BTs are always running up-to-date programsStructure for personal growth: BTs are provided with a clear pathway to grow in the ABA field. We also support our BTs' individual interests and provide opportunities for them to pursue these interests at TLBC.Focus on Staff: The happiness of our staff is essential to the quality of service that TLBC provides. TLBC is constantly evolving to ensure our staff's happiness through an extensive benefits package, supportive mentors and supervisors, and frequent opportunities for promotions and raises.What makes you a great fit for TLBC:Enthusiastic about TLBC’s mission and the success of its clientsStrong organization skillsCollaborativeStrong interpersonal skillsExperience working with childrenOpen to obtaining RBT certification within 90 days of employment (training provided)Ability to work afternoons (3:00-6:00pm) a minimum of three days per weekBenefits:The RBT position is a W-2 position with the following benefits for full-time employees:Competitive hourly ratePaid Time OffSick LeaveFlexible hoursMedical Insurance for full-time staff401(k) with a 4% company matchShort-term Disability Insurance for full-time staffInitial as well as Ongoing TrainingIn-house RBT TrainingTablet for Electronic Data CollectionPaid trainingsMileage PayFrequent Support & SupervisionContinuing Education reimbursementAccess to TLBC materials, curriculums, and gamesOpportunities for growth within the companyFor more information about our company or our staff, check out our website at www.tl-bc.comJob Type: Part-timeBenefits: 401(k)401(k) matchingDental insuranceFlexible scheduleHealth insurancePaid time offTuition reimbursementVision insurance

If you claim membership, license, certification, or credentials, you must submit a copy of said document in your application package. Check the Education section above to see what is allowed and what is required. Any claims you make in your resume regarding education or degrees MUST be supported by submitting with your application official or unofficial transcripts or a list of courses, grades earned, completion dates, and quarter and semester hours earned issued from your school. You may submit a copy your degree(s) if specific coursework does not have to be verified. Are you a veteran claiming 5-point veterans' preference or claiming sole survivorship preference?
